Traders from border areas who wished to remain anonymous, as well as entrepreneurs with experience of informal “re-exports” through Georgia using channels that have existed since the 1990s, say that price and quality could eventually become the decisive factors. However, this process could take years.

Practical obstacles and possible timeframes

Issues surrounding certification, phytosanitary controls, customs procedures, bank transfers and insurance have yet to be fully resolved.

Logistics currently operate mainly through Georgia. Direct rail links and the TRIPP corridor are still at the infrastructure development stage. Competition also remains high, with suppliers from Turkey, Russia and Iran already present in the market alongside domestic producers. The competitiveness of Armenian goods will therefore depend on their price, quality and logistics costs.

Under an optimistic scenario, small-scale shipments of industrial goods and raw materials could begin within several months to a year. A more realistic scenario would see trade gradually expand over one to three years, while under a pessimistic scenario, political fluctuations and public reaction could delay the process considerably.

What to watch next

Key indicators could include the first genuine commercial shipments from Armenia appearing in customs statistics, the introduction of banking mechanisms for cross-border payments, official approval of a list of potential goods for trade, and changes in the procurement policies of retailers such as Bravo, Araz and others.

Independent polling and sociological research in both countries will also be needed to assess public attitudes towards goods labelled “Made in …”. Without such data, statements about future trade will remain largely expressions of intent.

World.title: ‘From crisis management to stability’: Pashinyan unveils new government programme
World.content:
Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

The Armenian government has approved its programme for 2026-2031. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said it marked a shift from crisis management to stability. Looking back on his eight years as prime minister, he said the coronavirus pandemic, followed by the war and the post-war situation, had forced the government to operate in crisis-management mode. Now that Armenia and Azerbaijan have established peace, the government can “return to the unfinished part of the agenda of the 2018 Velvet Revolution”.

The new programme focuses on stability, he said. Pashinyan stressed that it rests entirely on the concept of “Real Armenia” and the principles underpinning the establishment of the Fourth Republic.

In 2025, the ruling Civil Contract party announced a new strategic goal: establishing the Fourth Republic of Armenia. The party congress unanimously adopted a declaration to this effect. According to the document, the Fourth Republic “will be based on the concept of preserving the internationally recognised sovereign territory of the Republic of Armenia, covering 29,743 sq km, in accordance with the 1991 Alma-Ata Declaration”. The declaration says the party reached this decision after analysing the history of the Third Republic. The Third Republic refers to the present-day Republic of Armenia, which declared independence following a nationwide referendum in 1991. The First Republic refers to the republic proclaimed on 28 May 1918. Accordingly, Soviet Armenia is considered the Second Republic.

“Following the 7 June 2026 election, the ideology of ‘Real Armenia’ won. This means it has become the official ideology. Armenia is therefore entering the stage of its history that we call the Fourth Republic. We must continue and give new momentum to democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms,” the prime minister stressed.

Government plans for the next five years

According to the new programme, the Armenian government will pursue the following goals in 2026-2031:

strengthening and further institutionalising the peace established between Armenia and Azerbaijan;

maintaining and further developing a favourable security environment around Armenia, in particular by normalising and developing relations with countries in the region and deepening existing partnerships beyond it;

unblocking Armenia through the Crossroads of Peace project and the “Trump Route” (TRIPP) transit programme;

liberalising the visa regime with the EU for Armenian citizens;

deepening democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms.

With whom does Yerevan plan to deepen partnerships under its “balanced foreign policy”?

In 2026-2031, the Armenian government will pursue a “balanced and proportionate” foreign policy.

“It has proved effective in stabilising Armenia’s external environment. Regionalisation plays a key role in foreign policy, whose goal is to ensure conditions in which Armenia can not only live without external support, but do so comfortably,” the document says.

Based on this approach, the government places particular importance on further developing relations with Georgia, Iran, Turkey and Azerbaijan. The government has outlined the following steps for each neighbouring country:

Georgia

Yerevan will continue implementing the measures set out in the Declaration on Establishing a Strategic Partnership between Armenia and Georgia. This will create new mutually beneficial opportunities for political, trade, economic, energy and transport cooperation, as well as regional and joint infrastructure projects.

Iran

Armenia will continue energy cooperation with Iran, develop cross-border infrastructure and expand transport routes through Iran, including North-South and Persian Gulf-Black Sea corridors.

Turkey

The Armenian government will continue efforts to establish diplomatic relations with Turkey, open the Armenian-Turkish border and put at least two modern border crossing points into operation. It also plans to restore and expand transport, energy and digital infrastructure, as well as bilateral and multilateral trade.

Azerbaijan

The government plans to continue efforts to sign and ratify a peace agreement and carry out work on the delimitation and demarcation of the state border. Contacts between civil society and business communities in the two countries will continue, helping to establish bilateral trade.

The foreign policy priorities specifically include deepening strategic partnerships with the European Union, the US, France and China. With Russia, Armenia plans to “transform and deepen its partnership”.

Against the backdrop of tensions over the ban on Armenian food and other exports to Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), which Russia leads, the programme says:

“Work will continue to ensure the full and uninterrupted exercise of the EAEU’s fundamental freedoms — the free movement of labour, services, goods and capital — as well as to develop relations with member and observer states.”

Regarding relations with the European Union, the programme stresses that Armenia will continue working to meet standards in democracy and the rule of law, as well as in the economic, financial and other spheres.

Armenia intends to deepen its partnership with the United States further. Cooperation will continue based on the principles set out in the Strategic Partnership Charter and bilateral memorandums of understanding.

“The TRIPP project, the ‘Trump Route’, will be implemented, at least in terms of operating energy and railway infrastructure, while integrating Armenia into major regional infrastructure projects,” the programme says.

Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

World.title: Parrots Rocky and Kiki: Tbilisi Zoo’s brightest residents – video
World.content:
Macaws at Tbilisi Zoo

Tbilisi Zoo is home to two species of macaws: scarlet macaws (Ara macao) named Rocky and Kiki, and blue-and-yellow macaws (Ara ararauna) named Chico and Paco. Their bright plumage catches visitors’ attention at first sight.

The macaws at Tbilisi Zoo are currently in the middle of their breeding season. Chico and Paco are expecting chicks. They usually incubate their eggs for 24–28 days. During this period, both parents actively protect and care for their future offspring.

Rocky and Kiki have become particularly cautious during this period. They often hide from people and rarely leave their enclosure. If you are planning to visit them at the zoo, keep in mind that they may be difficult to spot at the moment.

Macaws are known for their strong bonds. Pairs almost always stay together: they preen each other’s feathers, look for food together and protect each other when danger threatens.

With proper care, macaws can live for 50–60 years, and sometimes even longer — more than 70 years. Rocky’s exact age is unknown, but he is the oldest parrot at Tbilisi Zoo. Despite his advanced age, Rocky still has the same short-tempered and grumpy nature he has always had.

Once, when a keeper was a little late with a treat — a nut — Rocky immediately made his “protest” known by biting him on the finger. Because of their powerful beaks, macaw bites can be very painful and may cause serious injuries.

Macaws are incredibly intelligent birds. They have excellent memories, and some can even imitate human voices and words.

Although macaws are often kept as pets, caring for them is no easy task. They need plenty of space, daily attention, mental stimulation and constant variety in their surroundings.

It was founded on 10 February 1927 on the basis of the Caucasian Society for the Acclimatisation of Animals, which had been keeping wild animals since the early 20th century, though without official zoo status. World.title: Opinion from Abkhazia: ‘Nika Gvaramia said nothing new about resolving Georgian-Abkhaz conflict’
World.content:
An interview with Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Georgian opposition, about ways to resolve the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict attracted considerable attention in Georgia. In Abkhazia, however, it attracted almost no attention.

In his blog, Inal Khashig, editor of the Abkhaz newspaper Chegemskaya Pravda, offered his view on why. He believes the lack of interest among Abkhaz people is mainly because Gvaramia said nothing new in the interview and offered none of the things Abkhaz people would want to hear.

Inal Khashig: “From my strictly Abkhaz perspective, Gvaramia did not say anything radically new. If anything, he simply revived the old idea of resolving the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict through Georgia’s integration into the European Union, which would serve as an attractive incentive for Abkhaz people.

Georgian politicians have periodically put forward this idea since the presidency of Mikheil Saakashvili. The most recent was Georgia’s current prime minister, Irakli Kobakhidze, who in 2024 even set a specific deadline for achieving the goal. ‘Georgia will join the European Union together with our Abkhaz and Ossetian brothers by 2030,’ he declared at the time from a high-profile podium. In short, the EU idea has already been discussed many times.”

From Gvaramia’s interview, I also understood that Georgia cannot resolve the conflict through military means at present because it lacks the resources needed to guarantee the desired outcome. In this context, economic development and shared security interests should form the basis for resolving the conflict.

The only “new” idea proposed by the opposition politician is that Georgia needs to overcome the trauma it suffered after the Georgian-Abkhaz war of the 1990s because these memories “prevent it from moving forward and hold back development”. And on this point, I completely agree with Nika Gvaramia.

In my view, Georgia’s constant insistence on the need to regain Abkhazia is actually a heavy burden that prevents the country from achieving its full potential.

It is like a man who devotes all his energy and the rest of his life to trying to win back a wife who left him long ago. You can consider his life wasted.

I am convinced that if Mikheil Saakashvili had not abandoned his reform agenda in favour of “restoring territorial integrity” during his presidency, Georgia would almost certainly have made much greater progress in building its statehood.

I can well imagine that when Nika Gvaramia speaks about the need to overcome the trauma, he actually means giving up once and for all on claims to the lost territories. But as a politician, he understands the consequences of making such an admission openly.

As for the idea of restoring trust between Abkhaz people and Georgians, Gvaramia talks about this as well. But his understanding of “trust” is not very different from that of other Georgian politicians: essentially, “we will open up the world to you and shower you with benefits, but first come back to us”. In other words, it is a kind of bargain, with no guarantee that the other side is not bluffing.

But genuine trust looks very different.

In my view, a tangible step towards beginning the process of rebuilding trust between Abkhaz people and Georgians would be for Tbilisi to abolish the discriminatory Law on Occupied Territories, which does little short of preventing Abkhazia and South Ossetia from breathing freely without Georgia’s permission. But Nika Gvaramia did not mention this law even once. Perhaps that is why his interview went unnoticed in Abkhazia.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.



Nika Gvaramia interview

World.title: Opinion: ‘Removing Kobakhidze would be logical move for Ivanishvili if prime minister does not move against him first’
World.content:
Opinion on Georgian Prime Minister Kobakhidze

According to Eka Gigauri, executive director of Transparency International Georgia, removing Prime Minister Kobakhidze could eventually become a logical step for Ivanishvili — provided the prime minister does not manage to seize political power himself.

Eka Gigauri: “The Garibashvili case has once again confirmed what we already knew:”

None of this has anything to do with fighting corruption. Ivanishvili is reshuffling his inner circle, while Kobakhidze — with his approval and Mdinaradze’s assistance — is getting rid of political rivals. In “Georgian Dream”, no one is surprised when people enrich themselves at the public’s expense or engage in corruption: they all steal. The entire system is built on corruption, and Ivanishvili gave them the freedom to do so. So the “fight against corruption” is merely a staged performance designed to conceal a settling of scores. Kobakhidze does not get his hands dirty himself. He has Mdinaradze to do that for him, who has become his loyal executor and servant. It is obvious that the overwhelming majority of “Georgian Dream” supporters genuinely support Garibashvili. The same cannot be said of Kobakhidze and Mdinaradze. Look at the reactions from “Dream” supporters to statements by Garibashvili and his wife. If the authorities imprisoned Mdinaradze and then Kobakhidze, “Dream” supporters would not say a word in their defence. To them, Kobakhidze is still a former NGO worker and employee of international organisations. He is not a churchgoer and has no particular ties to the Church. The same applies to much of his team. There is no friendship, brotherhood or willingness to support one another in the “Georgian Dream” party. Apparently, none of them possesses that quintessential Georgian sense of honour. Out of fear of Bidzina, and now of Kobakhidze as well, they will betray one another, throw each other under the bus and abandon one another in times of trouble. Ivanishvili is deliberately deepening divisions within his own team and turning its members against one another. His goal is to prevent them from uniting against him and to force them to constantly undermine and confront each other. Today, Kobakhidze is clearly Ivanishvili’s favourite. However, he appears to have been carried away by this status. He often talks about his personal achievements, as though he had the power to act even without Ivanishvili. He may not have many genuine supporters within “Georgian Dream”, but today he exercises almost complete control over state institutions. “Georgian Dream” members appear to fear Kobakhidze greatly — perhaps even more than Bidzina. They know that Kobakhidze has direct access to Bidzina and can tell him something about a fellow party member that could ultimately destroy them. Even Garibashvili did not have this kind of influence. Kobakhidze has placed his people almost everywhere, while parliament is under his complete control. He has gradually concentrated enormous power in his hands. If this continues, even Ivanishvili may find it difficult to dismantle the system.

The experience of authoritarian regimes around the world also shows that dictators manage their inner circles according to the principle of “divide and rule”. They periodically replace their favourites and involve everyone in corruption schemes and other crimes, so that they can later use their weaknesses and complicity against them. At the same time, they pit influential groups against one another and keep everyone in a constant state of fear through selective punishment.

Thus, no individual or group can accumulate enough power to pose a real threat to the leader. However, such a system also carries a significant risk: a favourite who has concentrated all the levers of power in their hands may eventually begin building an independent political force. That is why dictators often get rid of their most loyal and influential allies.

At the same time, members of an authoritarian ruler’s inner circle often initiate changes of power. In other words, autocrats and dictators have good reason to fear their own inner circles. Today, if Kobakhidze wanted to, he could even remove Bidzina, and no one in “Georgian Dream” would dare oppose him. Therefore, removing Kobakhidze would eventually become a perfectly logical step — unless he managed to remove Ivanishvili first.

Opinion on Georgian Prime Minister Kobakhidze

World.title: Azerbaijan reports increase in trade turnover with China
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 23. The volume of trade between Azerbaijan and China totaled $2.610 billion in the first seven months of this year.

According to Trend’s calculations based on data from the State Customs Committee, this is $107.3 million, or 4.3%, more than the same period in 2025.

Over the reporting period, trade with China accounted for 8.93% of Azerbaijan’s total trade volume. Thus, China ranked fourth among the countries with which Azerbaijan conducts the largest volume of trade.

In the first seven months of this year, Azerbaijan exported goods worth $68.4 million to China. This is $15.1 million, or approximately 28.3%, more than the same period last year.

During the reporting period, Azerbaijan imported goods from China worth $2.542 billion, which is $122.3 million, or 3.8%, more than the same period in 2025. Thus, China ranked first on the list of countries from which Azerbaijan imports the largest volume of goods.

Overall, economic and trade relations between Azerbaijan and China are developing rapidly. Bilateral cooperation is not limited to trade alone. Recently, relations have also been expanding in the financial sector, capital markets, payment systems, energy, geological exploration, and agriculture. In this context, the prospects for cooperation between the Central Bank of Azerbaijan and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) were discussed, and SOCAR and the Chinese company BGP Inc. continued their efforts to implement joint projects and expand their partnership.

In addition, the agreements reached on granting access for Azerbaijani hazelnut and almond products to the Chinese market are of great importance for increasing non-resource exports between the two countries.

One of the key areas of cooperation between Azerbaijan and China is the development of the Middle Corridor. Azerbaijan’s strategic geographical location and its transportation and logistics capabilities enhance the importance of this route, which connects China with European markets. In recent years, expanded cooperation within the framework of the Baku-Tbilisi-Kars railway, the Baku International Sea Trade Port, and other transportation infrastructure projects has contributed to an increase in freight volumes along the Middle Corridor and to the strengthening of the region’s transit potential.

In this regard, transportation and logistics links are becoming one of the key areas of cooperation between Azerbaijan and China. Azerbaijan plays a key role as a transit country within the "Belt and Road" initiative, and the Middle Corridor (Trans-Caspian International Transport Route) offers an alternative and secure route for freight transport between China and Europe. The Middle Corridor serves as an alternative to both the Northern Route through Russia and the maritime route. Reports by the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank identify this corridor as a strategic alternative in terms of risk diversification. Azerbaijan, in turn, serves as a hub for multimodal transport along this route, a key organizer of the Caspian crossing, and a platform for implementing solutions in the areas of real-time monitoring and digital logistics. All of this has significantly increased global attention and interest in the country, and joint efforts to develop the Middle Corridor have become of exceptional importance for its further advancement.

Incidentally, since Azerbaijan is considered one of the key countries along this transport route, it has also managed to attract China’s interest. Thus, in October 2025, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed between Azerbaijan Railways CJSC and the Chinese port of Xi’an. The document provides for the expansion of multimodal transport, the optimization of container trains, and real-time monitoring of freight shipments.

Significant growth in freight volumes has also been recorded along the Middle Corridor. Over the past six years, freight volumes along the Middle Corridor have increased fivefold, exceeding 4 million metric tons per year. This was made possible primarily by the development of maritime transport and improvements to port infrastructure.

The further development of the corridor, in the context of shared interests, may allow for an even greater increase in its capacity in the future.

One of the main areas of cooperation between Azerbaijan and China is the energy sector. Cooperation in the energy sector is not limited to investment projects but has become one of the main pillars of the country’s sustainable development strategy. It is already clear that Azerbaijani-Chinese energy cooperation has moved beyond the traditional energy sector and entered the stage of the "green" transition. This aligns with both Azerbaijan’s climate goals for 2030 and 2050 and China’s global strategy for exporting "green" technologies. Projects such as the "Khizi-Absheron" wind farm (WF) and the "Gebustan" solar power plant (SPP) demonstrate that Chinese companies act not only as contractors but also as technological and financial partners.

One of the key areas of Azerbaijani-Chinese economic cooperation is the localization of industry and "green" energy technologies. In this context, the Alat Free Economic Zone (FEZ) is emerging as a new platform for industrial partnership between the two countries. "Sunsync" the first Chinese company officially registered in the zone, is preparing to establish a solar panel manufacturing facility there.

Valeh Alasgarov, chairman of the board of directors of the authorized body of the Alat Free Economic Zone, stated in an exclusive interview with Trend that the company will first introduce its cutting-edge technologies in Azerbaijan and build a solar panel manufacturing plant covering an area of 23 hectares in the Alat Free Economic Zone. According to him, the majority of the products manufactured will be exported, and the goal is to reach not only the domestic market but also international markets.

"From day one, our goal has been to enter not only the Azerbaijani market but also the global market. We recommend that investors use solar panels manufactured in the Alyat Free Economic Zone for installation on the roofs of businesses operating here. At the same time, the company will be able to participate in all relevant tenders held in Azerbaijan," said Valeh Alasgarov.

He noted that once Sunsync begins production, it will be more convenient for companies building solar power plants in Azerbaijan to source panels from within the country, both logistically and cost-wise.

"We have also offered the company a plot of land for the construction of a solar power plant in the Alat Free Economic Zone. Thus, using the panels manufactured here, it will be possible to sell the ‘green energy’ produced at the plant to enterprises operating in the Alat Free Economic Zone," he added.

World.title: Kazakhstan’s e-commerce market surges over three years
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 23. Kazakhstan's e-commerce market grew by more than 50% over three years, reaching 3.7 trillion tenge ($8.00 billion) in 2025 compared with 2.4 trillion tenge (about $5.19 billion) in 2023.

This was announced in a report published by the Kazakh Ministry of Trade and Integration.

According to the Ministry, the share of online sales in total retail trade also increased from 12.7% in 2023 to 14.3% in 2025.

"Marketplaces have become the main driver of the sector, accounting for 86% of total retail e-commerce in Kazakhstan. Platforms such as Kaspi.kz, Ozon, Wildberries, Halyk Market and Forte Market have contributed to the expansion of online trade, providing consumers with access to a wider range of goods and businesses with access to customers across the country", the ministry said.

Consumer preferences are also changing, with online purchases extending beyond electronics and clothing.

In 2025, phones and gadgets accounted for 17.1% of marketplace sales, followed by clothing, footwear and sporting goods at 12.4%, home and garden products at 12.1%, household appliances at 10.3% and food products at 7.4%.

The development of e-commerce is also changing delivery patterns. While consumers previously expected orders to arrive within several days, express delivery for certain product categories can now take less than an hour.

The e-grocery segment, covering the delivery of food and everyday consumer goods, is also expanding rapidly.

In 2025, five dark store projects were launched in Almaty, Astana, Karaganda and Aktobe. Marketplaces also installed 2,300 new parcel lockers to facilitate order collection.

As Kazakhstan's e-commerce market expands, the government is also developing digital infrastructure aimed at making trade more efficient. One of the key elements of this new trade architecture is the National Product Catalogue (NPC), Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Trade and Integration Aset Nusupov told Trend in an exclusive interview.

"The National Product Catalogue (NPC) is, without exaggeration, a large-scale infrastructure project for Kazakhstan's trade sector. I would like to emphasize that the NPC is not a one-time control measure. It is an element of the new trade architecture that is being formed in Kazakhstan. The NPC is a unified digital database where each product receives its own 'passport,' Nusupov said.

He explained that the digital product passport contains the product name and characteristics, as well as a unique national NTIN code - a 13-digit identifier that allows the product to be recognized in government and commercial information systems.

According to the vice minister, previously at least five different classification systems were used across various government systems. This resulted in the same product having different names in customs systems, statistics, and public procurement databases. "The NPC solves the problem of the so-called 'digital Babylon'. It consolidates data in one place, making it unified and reliable. This significantly simplifies business operations and makes the market more transparent," Nusupov noted.

He emphasized that the implementation of the NPC is particularly important for large product ecosystems, where goods turnover is rapid, while the origin and characteristics of products may often lack transparency. "The NPC brings the market to a qualitatively new level of transparency. A single source of data, logic, and identifiers creates a trusted environment for everyone - from manufacturers and businesses to end consumers," the vice minister said.

Dollar equivalents are calculated at the exchange rate of 1 USD = 462.22 tenge.

World.title: Live: Threats of SCG walkouts as Swans men's and women's teams take the field
World.content:
— reporting by Lucy McNally

Polly Burridge is a self-confessed Sydney Swans tragic, and co-host of independent podcast True Bloods.

"I've been a member of the club for 20 years. It's a huge part of my life. It's probably the biggest relationship I've been in apart from my family," she said.

Polly Burridge will attend both the AFLW and AFL matches today.

But this week's Swans scandal has rocked the club, and been very tough on its biggest supporters, like Burridge.

"I always felt like they stood for the right thing, like right now I'm wearing the women's Pride guernsey — we are multicultural, inclusive, we do the best by everyone, that's why I think this has been such a shock for everyone," she said.

"When the news broke, I don't think I've ever felt so much dread. In my lifetime, we've had four grand final losses, and this was 10,000 times that. I didn't think I would ever see this crest shown in this light and I think that's why it hurt so much."

But despite the pain, Burridge is planning to go to today's double-header; to watch both the men's and women's matches.

"At one point during this week I thought I'd just go for the girls then leave because it was at the point where the sanctions had not been handed down," she says.

"But now that the club has decided, I don't think it's fair to punish the boys who have done nothing wrong as they have also had their trust broken."

Polly Burridge is co-host of independent podcast True Bloods.

The Swans AFLW team play Essendon Bombers today.

Their coach Colin O'Riordan held a press conference on Friday alongside captain Lucy McEvoy, where he expressed his disappointment over the scandal, as well as his deep pride in the women's side.

McEvoy was then asked how she and her teammates were coping.

Polly Burridge said it's a shame the AFLW side has to deal with those questions.

"I understand why people want a women's perspective on this but at the same time they are still professionals, they still have a game to play and you need to let them do their job as opposed to being the beacon of hope for everyone," she said.

"Yes let's interview Callum Mills, let's not necessarily interview Lucy McEvoy, let's let her do her job and ask her a question about the football rather than 'how do you feel about the segregation between the two teams?'"

The podcast host said she is now excited to head to Moore Park today.

"I do think the girls will absolutely win … I do think they'll have a fantastic game," Burridge said.

"I think the boys who have been hurt are going to put in a good show. It's going to be a beautiful day of unity, a day the Swans fans will remember forever."

World.title: NT government pursues Fair Work action over firefighters, corrections dispute
World.content:
After more than a year of bargaining with the union representing firefighters and correctional officers, the NT government has filed two applications to the Fair Work Commission (FWC) in a move that could jeopardise its own public sector wages policy.

Earlier this year, the Commissioner for Public Employment applied to the FWC for two separate intractable bargaining declarations.

Under Commonwealth law, an intractable bargaining declaration could lead to the FWC independently deciding pay and conditions for workers, potentially forcing the government to abandon its policy of maximum 3 per cent wage rises for public sector workers.

The United Workers Union Northern Territory (UWU NT), which represents both firefighters and correctional officers, has challenged the applications, accusing the government of neglecting its duty.

"The government is not focusing on real negotiation and trying to improve public sector workers' conditions of employment," UWU NT secretary Erina Early said.

Erina Early says the government has not engaged in "real negotiation" but the commissioner for public employment disagrees. (ABC News: Tristan Hooft)

"They're more focused on litigation and legal proceedings."

But Commissioner for Public Employment Nicole Hurwood defended the applications.

In a statement, she said the UWU has rejected multiple offers for new enterprise agreements, including some informed by the FWC's recommendations.

Nicole Hurwood says the government's applications to the Fair Work Commission were necessary. (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

"The government has been clear with the UWU about the fiscal parameters within which it can negotiate," her statement read.

" The union continues to pursue claims that are significantly beyond what the government considers affordable or reasonable. "

Edith Cowan University lecturer in industrial relations Dr Alexis Vassiley said it was unusual to see governments applying for intractable bargaining declarations due to their unpredictable outcomes.

Alexis Vassiley says it is possible the FWC could give workers more than the 3 per cent pay rise. (ABC News: West Matteeussen)

"It's risky because what it does do is take the dispute out of the hands of the parties," he said.

"The Fair Work Commission isn't bound by the NT government's wages policy, so they could rule in favour of a much higher than 3 per cent increase."

Questions over cost as bargaining agreements bank up

Corrections officers and firefighters are two of seven workforces currently negotiating new enterprise agreements with the NT government.

The government is also negotiating with NT medical officers, dentists, nurses and midwives, Territory Generation and Power and Water Corporation employees.

Electrical Trades Union Northern Territory (ETU NT) organiser David Hayes said the pay offers made to Territory Generation and the Power and Water Corporation staff were "a joke."

"We've been offered a 2.75 per cent pay increase per year across the board, which is an absolute insult to those workforces," he said.

Union representatives Brendan Bussenschutt, David Hayes, Heidi Crisp and Erina Early are all fighting for better pay for workers. (ABC News: Tristan Hooft)

Australian Nursing and Midwifery Federation (ANMF) NT branch secretary Heidi Crisp said the policy of 3 per cent annual wage rises would hamper workforce numbers.

"People are having to resort to either being agency nurses or doing excessive overtime just to pay their regular bills," she said.

The ANMF NT is instead pursuing a 20.5 per cent wage increase over the next three years.

For union leaders such as Mr Hayes and Ms Crisp, the NT government's applications for intractable bargaining declarations involving corrections officers and firefighters set a worrying precedent.

The verdict on the application to the FWC for correctional officers will be handed down on September 2. (ABC News: Grace Atta)

Ms Early said pursuing this action against unions would be fiscally irresponsible.

"For the intractable bargaining process, [the government is] spending a lot of money on interstate lawyers to go up against firefighters and corrections officers," she said.

"This government has money to fight workers, but they have no money to invest in workers?"

The verdict on the application to the FWC for NT firefighters is set to be delivered on Wednesday. (ABC News: Mitch Woolnough)

In a statement, Ms Hurwood said the government was yet to spend any money on lawyers for its FWC hearings.

"No legal costs have been incurred to date, as the intractable bargaining declaration processes have only recently commenced," the statement read.

"Legal representation will be required as the matters progress, with the associated costs borne by the relevant agencies."

The FWC will hand down its verdict on the intractable bargaining declaration application for NT firefighters this Wednesday, August 26, while their verdict on corrections officers will be handed down on September 2.

World.title: Grafton 12yo takes campaign to politicians to fix beloved skate park
World.content:
When 12-year-old Haylee Blair found a problem that needed fixing, she decided to take action.

The avid skater from South Grafton, in northern NSW, was dismayed at the state of her local skate park.

"There's cracks and holes everywhere and glass and stuff all over the skate park," she said.

"I love skateboarding and it's a skate park for a reason, but we're using it as a bike track because it's too rough."



The Grafton Skate Park was first built in 1998, with expansions undertaken in 2001 and 2011.



The Clarence Valley Council's 2021 Draft Plan of Management for the skate park and other facilities noted the bowls had aged and its poor condition presented a safety hazard to users.

Haylee is a keen and active skater but says the Grafton park is not fit for purpose. (Supplied: Trudi Blair)

Haylee has a vision for a brighter future, and has been using the power of democracy to make it happen.

This week, she approached her local council and asked for action to deliver the much-needed maintenance.

"Our park is used by so many young people, and it means a lot to our community," she wrote.

The cracks and debris at the skate park are unsafe for skateboarders to ride over, Haylee says. (Supplied: Trudi Blair)

On Thursday, the council voted unanimously to take up Haylee's cause, with a staff report to be brought back before councillors by October.



Councillor Cristie Yager called for the report and put Haylee’s case to the council.



“Haylee and her family and now a very large group of people are getting behind the positivity that would come from having the skate park brought back up to a standard where it is suitable for skating," Cr Yager said at the council meeting on Thursday.



“I’m hoping we can get a whole lot of information that is available publicly that can help us find any kind of avenue forward on getting [the skate park] up to scratch.”



Cr Yager said that the upgrades to the Grafton skate park may not happen within this term of council.



Haylee said her desire is for future repairs to the park to have some additions to help skaters of all ages take up the sport.

"I would like to see a smoother skate park and maybe … a pump track for littler kids to have a go, because currently the ramps are way too big for little kids," she said.

"[Also some] shading and cameras."

It has been a sustained effort by the young skater, who first brought the issue to light on the community radio program she hosts after school.

That led to an invitation to present to a local rotary club, and then last month a conversation with her local mayor and member for state parliament.

Haylee is celebrating the council's vote. (Supplied: Trudi Blair)

Although supportive, Cr Ray Smith said the council did not have the funds for the estimated $250,000 project, and would need government assistance to pay for the work.

'That's community'

A little north from Haylee's hometown, the nearby regional city of Lismore shows how transformative a skate park can be.

Since opening a new state-of-the-art facility last August, Lismore has hosted several major skate events, including an official Skate Australia Olympic pathway event in April.

Even when major events are not running, the park is rarely empty.

Lismore's new skate park was widely anticipated and has been popular since it opened in 2025. (Supplied: Lismore City Council)

"I start coaching down there at 7:30 most mornings, and I'm always surprised, sometimes there's people there skating even before I get there," skate coach and skate shop owner Samual Izac said.

"And then into the evening, I'll be coaching two, three sessions in a row and then people keep turning up until the lights go off at 11."

Mr Izac said there were skaters as young as three or four, through to adults into their 50s.

"When you're bringing people of all ages and demographics together socially, that's a really good thing," he said.

"To me, that's community."

Samual Izak says a good skate park brings the community together. (Supplied: Lismore City Council)

Haylee hopes a refurbished or perhaps even a rebuilt skate park in Grafton could bring her own community together, especially younger people.

"It's so they can get out, have fun for free, exercise and get off their phones," she said.

World.title: Father leaves tired 7yo at station to continue climbing Mount Fuji
World.content:
A man who left his seven-year-old son behind for hours on Japan's Mount Fuji while continuing the climb, has received a stern warning from police according to local media.

The boy was found alone on a hiking route on Thursday and taken into police custody, a police officer in the Shizuoka region told news wires agency AFP.

The child told his father he was tired at the sixth station of the mountain, which is located at an altitude of more than 2,000 metres, local network SBS TV reported.

A gate was installed to prevent overcrowding and night climbing at Mount Fuji's fifth station. (AFP: Yoshinobu Goto/The Yomiuri Shimbun)

As his older brother had gone on ahead, the seven-year-old's father told him to "wait here" and carried on hiking with his other son, according to SBS.

TV Asahi said the boy was told to wait for eight hours with only snacks, a soft drink and no money.

They said staff at the mountain hut alerted police to his presence.

Officers contacted the father who was at the eighth station and handed the boy over to him when he returned.

The police officer told AFP officers gave the man a telling-off for leaving the child behind.

The father reportedly apologised to the police, admitting the act was careless.

Fatalities recorded in 2026 hiking season

Mount Fuji, an active volcano and Japan's highest mountain at 3,776 metres, is popular with both local and international hikers.

Authorities in 2024 implemented an entry fee and put a cap on numbers to try and prevent overcrowding.

Tourists need to book to climb Mount Fuji The new measures come into force after hundreds of thousands of people climbed the peak last year.

A Swiss man died last month after losing consciousness hiking up the mountain, while rescuers separately managed to save a 99-year-old woman after she was injured on the climb and sheltered in a hut overnight.

The Swiss climber's death was the second fatality since the Fuji hiking season began on July 1, after a 65-year-old Japanese man died on July 17, reportedly after falling and hitting his head.

More than 200,000 people climbed the mountain last year, down from about 220,000 in 2023.

There were nine deaths in the 2024 season but none in 2025.

ABC/AFP

World.title: Breaking: Australia records its first bird flu case in a mammal
World.content:
Australia's first case of bird flu in a mammal has been confirmed following testing of a long-nosed fur seal found in South Australia.

Federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins has told reporters in Hobart the seal was found at Beachport, 300 kilometres south of Adelaide.

"This is sadly our first confirmed case of H5 bird flu in a mammal in Australia," Ms Collins said.

"Although this is a concerning development, it is not unexpected for us to start to see infection in other wildlife, particularly in marine mammals, particularly in areas where there are high infection rates in wild birds.

"I have been advised that at this time the detection does not appear to be associated with other sick or dead marine mammals.

"An infection of this individual animal is likely to have occurred due to exposure to infected wild birds or the environment that they share."

Julie Collins announced the confirmed case at a media conference in Hobart. (ABC News)

There have now been 298 positive H5 bird flu events recorded in Australia since the outbreak, with 183 of those in South Australia.

"At this stage there is no evidence of infection in our poultry or agriculture systems," Ms Collins said.

The minister said she would be travelling to South Australia "in the coming days" to discuss the state's response to H5 bird flu.

She urged anyone who sees sick or dead birds not to touch them or get close to them but to record their location and make a report.

World.title: One Nation pursuing migration rate 'not too different' to Labor
World.content:
One Nation MP David Farley says immigration rates to Australia would not be "too different" to Labor or the Coalition under Pauline Hanson, as he suggested a figure close to the government's migration target of 225,000 by 2028.

Mr Farley told ABC Insiders One Nation would not seek to cut migration rates deeper than about 230,000 a year, saying the migration target would be a net overseas migration rate of about 130,000 plus "a minimum" 100,000 skilled workers under established visa schemes.

The net overseas migration (NOM) rate accounts for the total number of people entering Australia with plans to stay at least a year minus those leaving, including those entering on visa programs such as working holiday-maker visas, the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility scheme, and skilled worker visas.

Mr Farley admitted once One Nation's "true NOM" and skilled visa targets were combined, its migration rate of about 230,000 would be similar to figures already forecast by the government.

"The raw number is not too different, but the reality is where do we need them. We don't need them in the great urban 'metroplex'. We need them out to be productive, working out in agriculture, engineering, mining, etc," Mr Farley said.

"The big difference is we are focusing on what are the skills we need as a nation."

Everybody wants to cut migration The causes of migration are murky and it is harder for politicians to control than they would like to admit.

Mr Farley said One Nation was focused on net migration "in its true form", plus workers from several necessary visa programs, citing about 40,000 migrants under the Pacific workers visa, about 68,000 to 70,000 skilled aged care migrants and skilled mechanical and engineering workers.

He said that category would make up "a minimum" of 100,000 more visas granted each year under a One Nation government, on top of what he described as the "true" net overseas migration rate of 130,000.

While the government has forecast migration returning to about 225,000 by 2028, it has repeatedly overshot those forecasts, particularly after the reopening of international borders following the COVID-19 pandemic.

The One Nation MP's comments follow weeks of debate on how deeply migration rates should be cut, an issue that has become a political battleground in part because of One Nation's rise in popularity on a platform of slashing migration.

The party has also laid out its intentions to restrict migration from some countries deemed to be higher risk, suggesting it could use travel advice to determine which countries should be affected by migration restrictions.

The Coalition has been developing a migration policy to combat One Nation, as the right wing party has emerged from the fringe of politics to threaten the Coalition's status as the opposition.

While it has not yet set migration targets, the Coalition intends to tie migration to housing construction rates, saying that migration rates will be restricted to the pace of housing completions in the previous year in order to close the supply shortfall in the housing sector.

The government, meanwhile, has been planning reforms to further tightening of temporary visas as it seeks to bring down net overseas migration from 300,000 to its goal of 225,000 by 2028.

Those reforms were postponed, with the policy still to be settled by cabinet.

In July, the government issued a directive to prioritise people already onshore for visa processing, slowing arrivals overseas — including for in-demand skilled workers in nursing, teaching and elsewhere.

Business fears race to bottom on migration

With both major parties and One Nation competing on migration, business groups have stepped up their calls for "stability" in the migration system, fearing a race to the bottom could leave industries with deeper worker shortages.

On Friday, the Australian Industry Group said skilled migration was "essential" to addressing workforce shortages in housing, infrastructure, manufacturing, health, aged care and in emerging industries.

"Australia cannot meet current and future workforce needs through domestic training alone," chief executive Innes Willox said.

"Reducing skilled migration at a time of persistent workforce shortages would put further pressure on housing delivery, major infrastructure projects and business investment."

The industry group urged that permanent skilled migration remain at current levels, and asked for visa processing and skills recognition processes to be sped up.

It also asked for the government to do more to explain to voters how migration supports essential services and the economy.

World.title: WA by-election puts One Nation's growing appeal to the test
World.content:
What's more likely: Angus Taylor becoming prime minister or Basil Zempilas coaching the West Coast Eagles?

It sounds like the set-up to a joke, but it was a question effectively posed by Zempilas himself on Tuesday morning.

While attacking Labor for failing to secure a firm commitment from the prime minister on WA's share of the GST, he was asked whether he would seek the same assurances from his federal leader.

"Well, he's not the prime minister," Zempilas shot back.

"He could be," a reporter replied.

"He could be, and I could be the coach of the West Coast Eagles as well," Zempilas retorted.

Basil Zempilas seemingly compared his prospects of becoming the Eagles coach to Angus Taylor becoming prime minister. (ABC News: Keane Bourke )

There are plenty of parallels between the struggling Liberals and the floundering Eagles, but it's safe to say Zempilas wasn't exactly talking up Taylor's chances of leading the country.

One Nation: Friend or foe?

Labor's attacks wrote themselves.

"The leader of the opposition got out the white flag and waved it for Angus Taylor," Deputy Premier Rita Saffioti told parliament later that day.

" But we know that he is very used to waving the white flag because he has waved the white flag … in Secret Harbour. He wants One Nation to win. "

It's a claim Labor has made throughout the by-election campaign, and one that Zempilas has strenuously denied each time.

Rita Saffioti has accused Basil Zempilas of wanting One Nation to win the Secret Harbour by-election. (ABC News: Keane Bourke )

"The ultimate win for us will be [Liberal candidate] Ryan Robertson joining us in parliament," he said on Monday, as pre-polling began.

"But will Labor losing a seat that they have always held also be a victory for us? Yes, it will."

Whether it's surrendering to One Nation or being realistic about his party's chances, the Liberals are certainly not opposing the prospect of the minor party taking the seat.

Zempilas was happy to chat with One Nation's candidate Luke Herdegen at the early voting centre, and the Liberals' social media has not criticised — or even mentioned — Herdegen.

Basil Zempilas chatting to Luke Herdegen at the early voting centre. (ABC News: Keane Bourke )

On the one hand, it's an understandable response. For the Liberals to even dream of winning the seat, they would need One Nation preferences, so they cannot afford to upset the party.

On the other hand, One Nation poses a threat to the Liberals' very existence. Just look at South Australia, where two of the four seats One Nation won at the March election were taken directly from the blue team.

First WA test for One Nation

Western Australia is vastly different to the east coast, where One Nation has surged in opinion polls, and South Australia, where they've been tested at the ballot box.

Next Saturday's Secret Harbour by-election will be the first real test of whether the party's popularity is also rising across the Nullarbor.

The poll is expected to challenge Labor's stronghold on the rapidly growing, mortgage-belt seat, where a mix of older Western Australians and young families struggling with the cost of living reside.

Pre-polling for the Secret Harbour by-election opened on Monday. (ABC News: Keane Bourke )

Former Labor treasurer Ben Wyatt explained one reason why One Nation may be appealing to voters in Secret Harbour.

"If you oversell your capacity as a government to solve the problems of the world for people and you can't do it, because inevitably you can't do all those things, you create dissatisfaction," he told a business breakfast on Wednesday.

"I think there is a real opportunity now, and Australians would be receptive to it — just a bit of an honest conversation of what is the role of government."

Ben Wyatt says One Nation is capitalising on voter dissatisfaction with government. (ABC News: Keane Bourke )

Perhaps that is part of what voters see in One Nation.

"The political system in this country needs shaking up. Labor and Liberal just take voters for mugs, basically," one early voter told reporters this week.

"I think we've just had this government in for too long, so just need a bit of change," another Secret Harbour resident said.

What kind of change?

"Just across the board, a bit of everything I think — just fresh people, fresh eyes," he said.

'Wave of poison'

Premier Roger Cook acknowledged there was "no doubt" One Nation would take votes off Labor when the counting began, and that his party could "absolutely" lose the seat.

"In addition to the fact that you have this usual pattern of swings away from governments during by-elections, you also have this situation where you've got this wave of poison coming from the One Nation debate on the east coast," he told 102.5 ABC Perth.

Roger Cook has acknowledged Labor is facing a battle to retain Secret Harbour. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

The member being replaced in the by-election, former Labor MP Paul Papalia, said he understood it was "enticing to have a whinge and complain about things", but no solutions had been offered.

"I hope people recognise we've had good, solid government in Western Australia. It's the best state in the country. You don't want to jeopardise that," he said.

Lessons to be learned

The responses capture the two messages Labor has been trying to stick to when it comes to One Nation: condemning the party, while sympathising with the pressures facing its supporters.

The risk is the condemnation is louder and pushes them further into One Nation's arms.

Labor wants to bind the Coalition to its One Nation fight Labor is increasingly trying not to simply attack One Nation, but binding Pauline Hanson and the Coalition together in voters' minds as partners in a shared agenda.

One Nation's WA leader, Rod Caddies, accused Labor of running a "ridiculous campaign" based on "smears" and "gutter politics".

The effect of that will be one of the key lessons for Labor to take away from this campaign.

For the Liberals, it will be an important guide as to whether they should work with One Nation to benefit from their preferences, or whether they too need to attack.

That's what the Liberal MP in the overlapping federal seat, Andrew Hastie, believes as he prepares for a "dirty and nasty" fight.

"We've got to focus on who we are as Liberals, and that is what we're doing," he told RN Breakfast.

Andrew Hastie's federal seat overlaps Secret Harbour. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

Given the party's precarious position already, it's an urgent question for the Liberals to find the answer to.

If he doesn't find the right answer though, at least Zempilas might have another career change left in him.

"I was in league footy," he laughed. "It wouldn't be that big a stretch."

World.title: Man driving stolen vehicle killed in head-on crash
World.content:
A man who stole two cars has been killed after colliding with other vehicles in Melbourne overnight.

The 46-year-old man from Melton was driving a stolen white Subaru on the wrong side of the road when he collided with two other cars near Punt Road and Boulton Parade about 9pm, according to police.

The man then got out of the Subaru and got into one of the vehicles he had collided with, a Mustang. The driver of the Mustang was not inside the car at the time and was uninjured, police reported.

Police said the man then drove the Mustang erratically onto Barassi Way in East Melbourne, colliding head on with two more vehicles — a Range Rover and a Toyota Camry — which resulted in him being ejected from the Mustang and dying at the scene.

The woman driving the Range Rover sustained an arm injury and was taken to hospital, but the other motorist was uninjured.

The Subaru initially driven by the man was stolen from Glen Iris on August 20, according to police, and was bearing false numberplates.

Brunton Avenue was closed to traffic while police examined the scene.

Anyone who witnessed the collision or who has dash-cam footage is urged to contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or submit a confidential report online.

More than an hour before the AFLW’s Sydney Swans are set to take on Essendon, dozens of die-hard fans queued up at the members’ gate.

“Go the Swannies, all of the Swans,” one woman is heard yelling.

“I’m proudly red and white until the day I’m in a box”.

World.title: Paul McManus was killed five years ago. His family is still waiting for justice
World.content:
NationalVictoriaCourts Paul McManus was killed five years ago. His family is still waiting for justice Eleanor Campbell August 23, 2026 — 11:39am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Every time she passes a green light at an intersection, Jennifer McManus thinks of her 40-year-old son Paul. In October 2021, the Melbourne-born tech engineer was riding home on his motorcycle from a James Taylor concert when a driver allegedly ran a red light and struck him at a busy intersection in San Francisco’s Mission District. Paul McManus’ family (from left): father Brian, sister Sarah, mother Jennifer and brother Dave. Eddie Jim He was taken to hospital with critical injuries after 11pm and died before midnight. The woman allegedly driving the grey Jeep Compass, Breanna Gordon, then aged 32, was charged with misdemeanour vehicular manslaughter and released from police custody.



The man in Gordon’s passenger seat – identified as her boyfriend at the time – fled the scene before police arrived due to having two active warrants out for his arrest, according to police allegations. Thousands of kilometres away in the Victorian town of Aireys Inlet, Jennifer McManus was in the shower after spending the day at the beach with her family when her daughter, Sarah, took a call from Paul’s wife, Fern, in California. Paul and Fern during their wedding in 2020. “I knew it was midnight there, and Fern wouldn’t usually ever call us, it was always Paul’s phone, so I instantly thought something was wrong,” Sarah recalls. “She was upset, and she said, ‘There’s been an accident’, and she was like, ‘Well, Paul’s dead’. Mum was in the shower, and we were just in shock.”



In San Francisco, Fern remembers going out to search for Paul when he didn’t return home that night. She recalls remaining oddly calm after arriving at the scene of the crash when she went out to look for him, a habit she picked up from her husband, whom she describes as “devastatingly funny” and one of the “most brilliant people I’ll ever know”. “He had this sort of code of behaviour where he would not freak out about anything before he had all the facts,” Fern says. “I remember when the worst imaginable happened, I found myself grateful that he had helped equip me with this toolkit of how to deal with horrible things.” Paul and his beloved dog, Huxley. The pair met in Mexico while travelling with friends a decade earlier and bonded over a conversation about the famous oceanographer Sylvia Earle. They were married for more than a year when he died. Six weeks after the crash, Gordon failed to appear for a court arraignment hearing and for three years the case lingered in pre-trial status due to a backlog of pending cases caused by COVID-19.



When the case was finally set for trial in June 2024, Gordon again failed to show in court and a bench warrant was issued for her arrest. Despite ongoing pleas to US authorities to track her down, family members say they were told there were not enough police resources to locate her. “She [Gordon] hasn’t had a period of not driving, that we know of,” Jennifer says. “She got her car back before Fern got Paul’s motorbike back from the insurance company.” A spokesperson for Gordon was contacted for comment. Frustrated, the McManus family considered hiring a private investigator for thousands of dollars but ultimately decided against it. After contacting the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs, they were told that nothing could be done to help them except lodging an overseas death certificate.



It was not until two years later, in May 2026, that Gordon was re-arrested on a bench warrant and brought back to San Francisco. Paul’s family says they learnt of the development from a journalist at The San Francisco Standard. “You would have thought the government would do more in the circumstances, but we haven’t heard anything since that,” Paul’s brother, Dave, says. Paul McManus’ family is still waiting for the case to go to the trial. Eddie Jim After almost five years in limbo, the family is now preparing for Paul’s case to go to trial by the end of October. Although they have since established regular contact with California’s district attorney, they remain deeply sceptical about the prospect of a swift resolution. Paul, who grew up in the Melbourne suburb of Eltham, is described by his loved ones as an adventurous, humble and fiercely unique spirit. He spent much of his childhood diving and spearfishing with siblings Dave, Sarah and older brother Luke.



“He should have been born with gills,” Dave says. “Paul did a lot for ocean conservation and a lot of his friends and network in San Francisco were a part of that.” A photo of Paul McManus in the water. His family says he was an adventurous, humble and free spirit who loved the ocean. The Age At the time of his death, he and his brother Dave were working on launching a seaweed farm to regenerate ocean habitats, a business his brother has since launched in his honour. Hundreds of people, including police officers who were at the scene of the crash, attended a funeral paddle-out ceremony in his honour at Dillon Beach, north of San Francisco, and at Point Roadknight on Victoria’s Surf Coast. Paul’s parents are clear about what justice looks like for their son.



“We just want simple justice and whatever it is – it needs be done in a fair way,” his father Brian says. Jennifer adds: “There should be some sort of rehabilitation program, that’s what Paul would have wanted. Just something worthwhile and putting something good back into the world.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.
